pageTitle: Sexual Harassment Prevention — Blue Seat Studios
heroTagline: Animated compliance training that sticks. Covers harassment, bystander intervention, and state-specific requirements for employees and managers.
coversBullets: Real-world scenarios that show what harassment looks like | Clear, relatable examples of what to do (and what not to do) | Humor that lowers defensiveness and helps the message land | Builds confidence to speak up, set boundaries, and step in
L1_desc: Your right to a respectful, harassment-free workplace. This video sets the foundation for what that means and why it matters.
L2_desc: Meet Stan and explore how person-to-person harassment shows up at work. Learn why intent doesn’t cancel out impact.
L3_desc: What is quid pro quo harassment? A memorable walkthrough of how power and pressure can cross the line.
L4_desc: How reporting works and why it’s okay to speak up. Covers protections from retaliation and manager responsibilities.
L5_desc: A light, memorable take on respect at work. Reinforces that no one should be made to feel lesser based on identity.
L6_desc: What creates a hostile work environment? An introduction to the key concepts and definitions.
L7_desc: A workplace interaction where someone sets a clear boundary. Shows what respectful behavior looks like in response.
L8_desc: When a power imbalance changes the situation. Explores how pressure from a supervisor can make something inappropriate.
L9_desc: A single serious incident can be enough. This scenario shows how severe behavior can create a hostile environment.
L10_desc: Harassment doesn’t have to come from inside your organization. Looks at ongoing, low-level behavior from a vendor.
L11_desc: Not every uncomfortable moment is harassment. Helps distinguish awkward from inappropriate.
L12_desc: Revisits the "severe or pervasive" standard. Introduces both subjective and objective perspectives.
L13_desc: How to take action when something feels off. Introduces practical options: direct, distract, delay, and delegate.
L14_desc: Covers California-specific laws under FEHA. Explains key protections and requirements.
L15_desc: Stan learned the key concepts of sexual harassment prevention. You’re ready to put them into practice.

Mental Health Support — Blue Seat Studios
heroTagline: Training that reduces stigma and gives everyone — not just HR — the language and confidence to support a colleague who's struggling.
coversBullets: Recognizing the signs of burnout, anxiety, and depression in yourself and others | How to start a supportive conversation without overstepping | Understanding what to say — and what not to say | When and how to refer someone to professional resources | Building a workplace or campus culture that normalizes help-seeking | Manager and faculty-specific responsibilities and boundaries
L1_desc: An introduction to mental health concepts — what they are, why they matter, and how they show up differently for different people.
L2_desc: How to notice when a colleague, student, or teammate may be struggling — without diagnosing or overstepping.
L3_desc: Practical language and frameworks for opening a supportive conversation with someone you're concerned about.
L4_desc: Common well-meaning responses that can backfire — and what to say instead.
L5_desc: When to refer someone to professional support, what resources to offer, and how to protect your own wellbeing in the process.

heroTagline: Honest education that meets students where they are — not where we wish they were. Focuses on real decisions, real risk, and real ways to look out for each other.
coversBullets: Understanding how alcohol affects decision-making and memory | Recognizing the difference between drinking and risky drinking | How to check in on a friend who may have had too much | Consent and alcohol — what the law says and what it means in practice | Bystander strategies for real party and social situations | Campus resources and how to use them without fear
L1_desc: How alcohol actually works — what it does to judgment, coordination, memory, and decision-making. No scare tactics. Just the real science.
L2_desc: The difference between drinking socially and drinking in ways that put yourself or others at risk — and how to tell the difference in the moment.
L3_desc: What the law says about consent when alcohol is involved — and why "I didn't know" isn't a defense.
L4_desc: How to recognize when someone has had too much, and what to actually do about it — without making it a big deal.
L5_desc: Campus resources explained — from counseling to medical amnesty policies. Why using them is always the right call.

heroTagline: Management isn't a personality type — it's a skill set. This course gives new and experienced managers the practical tools to set expectations, give feedback, and handle the conversations nobody wants to have.
coversBullets: Setting clear expectations and measurable goals | Giving feedback that actually changes behavior — positive and corrective | Having difficult conversations before they become HR issues | Understanding your legal obligations as a manager | Documenting performance fairly and consistently | Recognizing and avoiding bias in performance evaluations
L1_desc: The mindset shift from individual contributor to manager — and what your team actually needs from you.
L2_desc: How to set goals that are specific enough to be useful — and how to revisit them without micromanaging.
L3_desc: The difference between feedback that changes behavior and feedback that just makes people defensive. Frameworks that work in real situations.
L4_desc: How to address performance issues, attendance, attitude, and conflict directly — before small problems become big ones.
L5_desc: What managers must know about discrimination, retaliation, accommodation, and when to loop in HR.
